# Synthetic fixtures

Every file here is **invented**. Nothing is derived from a real book, and nothing comes from Kavita
or any other GPL project. They exist so the file-handling rules can be exercised against real
containers without touching a real library, and so the same bytes can be handed to the Lectern
reimplementation as its conformance fixtures.

The book is "Fixture Book" by "Fixture Author"; the series is "Fixture Saga"; the pages are
flat-colour PNGs. No file exceeds 9 KB.

## What is here

| File | Format | What it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| `sample.epub` | EPUB 2 | A bare EPUB: `mimetype` stored first, `META-INF/container.xml`, OPF, NCX, one chapter. `dc:title`, `dc:identifier`, `dc:language` only. |
| `sample-metadata.epub` | EPUB 2 | The same, plus `dc:creator`, `dc:date`, and `calibre:series` / `calibre:series_index` — the embedded-metadata precedence rule. |
| `sample.pdf` | PDF 1.4 | A minimal but structurally valid one-page PDF with a correct xref table. |
| `sample.cbz` | CBZ | A zip of three PNGs, no `ComicInfo.xml`. |
| `sample-comicinfo.cbz` | CBZ | The same pages plus a `ComicInfo.xml` (Series, Number, Volume, Title, Writer, Publisher, Year, Month, PageCount, Genre, LanguageISO, Manga). |
| `sample.zip` | ZIP | The same pages under the raw archive extension. |
| `sample.cb7` | 7z | The same pages, a real 7-Zip container. |
| `sample.7z` | 7z | As above, under the raw archive extension. |
| `sample.rar` | RAR 4 | A genuine RAR, store method. |
| `sample.cbr` | RAR 4 | As above, under the comic extension. |
| `sample-mislabelled.cbr` | ZIP | A **zip** carrying the `.cbr` extension. Real files do this constantly; the rule spec says all comic extensions must accept any of the three archive signatures, so the corpus needs the case. |
| `sample.mobi` | MOBI | A Kindle book, built with calibre. |
| `sample.azw` | MOBI | The same MOBI container under the older Kindle extension. |
| `sample.azw3` | AZW3 | A Kindle book, built with calibre. |

`sample.mobi` and `sample.azw3` were built earlier with calibre from synthetic content and are
unchanged. Everything else is generated by `make_fixtures.py` in this directory.

## Regenerating

```
python3 make_fixtures.py            # writes into this directory
```

The 7z containers need a 7-Zip CLI (`7zzs`, or set `SEVEN_ZIP`). Nothing else is required beyond
the Python standard library.

## The RAR files are hand-built

There is no RAR encoder available here, and the only one that exists is non-free, so
`make_fixtures.py` writes the RAR 4 container directly from the published layout (marker block,
main header, one file header per page, end-of-archive block, CRC16 per header and CRC32 per file).
Both `sample.rar` and `sample.cbr` list and test cleanly under `7zzs`.

## Verification

Each file was checked as the format it claims to be, not merely by its extension:

- `7zzs l` / `7zzs t` open and test `cb7`, `7z`, `rar`, `cbr`, `cbz` and `zip`;
- Python `zipfile` validates every entry's CRC, and the EPUBs' `mimetype` is the first entry and stored;
- the PDF's header, trailer and every xref offset resolve to a real object;
- the `.azw` carries a `BOOKMOBI` PalmDB header;
- the product's own readers parse them — `readEpubMetadata` returns Title/Language for `sample.epub`
  and Title/Writer/Year/Series/Number for `sample-metadata.epub`, and `readComicInfo` returns the full
  field set for `sample-comicinfo.cbz` and nothing for `sample.cbz`.
